newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Penoles Q1 earnings seen stable.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Penoles Q1 earnings seen stable.

text.p: The world's largest refined silver producer, Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA, should report stable first quarter earnings in peso terms and a slight increase in income in dollar terms, analysts said.
An average of three analysts estimated first quarter earnings per share 0.68 pesos, virtually unchanged from the 0.67 earnings per share reported during the same period of 1996.
A company spokesman said Penoles expected to announce first quarter earnings results between April 28-29.

"We expect a stronger report in dollar terms, but because of the stronger peso and inflation it leads to a negative comparison in peso terms," Santander Investment analyst Sandra Morfin said. She estimated $0.08 in earnings per share for the quarter compared with $0.07 in the year-ago period.
Penoles saw stable peso cut into its earnings, which are mostly in exports and consequently in dollars, plus lower gold and silver prices prices, analysts predicted.
"The net effect is not clear. Although prices were lower, significant volume increases should be able to offset them," Morfin said.
Possibly lower Penoles earnings did not bother analysts, however, although some said the company's recent trading price of about 37.40 could be a bit high.
Industry observers hailed the company's medium-term expansion, saying aggressive investment plans will continue to help the company counter flux in metal prices.
"Penoles has talked about a four year program to 2000. I think they's acting in frustration to the market's schizophrenia," Credit Lyonnais analyst David Bodenberg said.

As part of an acquisitions plan, Penoles acquired a majority stake in Peru's government-run La Oroya on Friday. The company plans to move new mines on line in 1998 and 1999 and boost its own-mined production levels.
This and other recent acquisitions have been hailed as providing medium-term value to shareholders and broadening Penoles' metals base.
"The companies strategic plans are to diversify geographically and boost basic metal production," Serfin Brokerage analyst Hector Novoa said.
